classification.difficultyReason: Use the intercept and horizontal guide to solve for two exact x-coordinates, then read the perpendicular height and subtract the x-coordinates to obtain the base.

content.prompt: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ be defined as in the diagram below. Find the area of $\triangle ABC$.

spec.sourceRegion: Printed page 237, Question 11 diagram below the stem
spec.description: A blue natural-logarithm curve on black axes, with four marked points, dashed guides, dashed side AC and an interior right-angle marker at B.
spec.mathematics: A is the curve's x-intercept. C is on both y=2 and y=ln(x). B is the projection of C onto the x-axis, and D is where the horizontal guide meets the y-axis. AB lies on the x-axis.
spec.answerVisibility: student-visible givens; derived coordinates and area are withheld

answer.worked:
At $A$, $\ln(x)=0$, so $A=(1,0)$. At $C$, $\ln(x)=2$, so $C=(e^2,2)$ and $B=(e^2,0)$. Thus $AB=e^2-1$ and $BC=2$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=\frac12\times AB\times BC\\\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=\frac12\times(e^2-1)\times2\\\text{Area of }\triangle ABC&=e^2-1\end{align*}$$
The area is $e^2-1$ square units.
